verdict_reason: The weighted score is 89/100, above the 85 pass mark, and no critical-severity findings were reported.
explanation: Every finding subtracts points from a perfect 100. Dependency CVEs cost 12 (critical), 6 (high), 1.5 (medium) or 0.3 (low); committed secrets cost the most (15/10/5/1); infrastructure misconfigurations cost 8/4/1/0.2; CodeQL security findings are weighted by the rule's CVSS-style security-severity score (0-10). Each category is capped (dependencies 45, secrets 25, IaC 10, code 40) so one noisy scanner cannot bury the result. A score of 85+ with zero critical findings is reported as secure.

category_why.vulnerability: a library you ship has a known, publicly documented flaw
category_why.secret: a credential appears to be committed in plain text
category_why.misconfiguration: deployment or infrastructure config weakens the runtime
category_why.code: CodeQL traced attacker-controlled data into a dangerous operation
category_why.code-quality: maintainability issue that makes future bugs more likely
